subject: Nanotechnology
title: Nanowire Field-Effect Sensors
description: A micro-lesson that makes Nanowire Field-Effect Sensors usable.

hook.text: A silicon nanowire acts like a transistor — charge from a binding molecule shifts the current measurably.

buildup.text: The nanowire channel is so thin that surface charges dominate — a single protein changes the gating field.

discovery.text: FET nanosensors detect DNA, proteins, and viruses in real time — no labels, no fluorescence needed.

twist.text: Ionic screening in blood shields the charge — the Debye length in physiological buffer is just 0.7 nm.

climax.text: Desalting steps and aptamer receptors shorten the distance — bringing the signal within Debye screening range.

punchline.text: A wire thinner than the target molecule feels it like a bump in the road.

quiz.question: Why is Debye screening a challenge for nanowire FET biosensors?
options: It causes the nanowire to corrode in salt solutions
Ions in solution shield the charge of bound molecules, weakening the electrical signal
It makes the nanowire too conductive to detect changes
